case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Protective Proceedings of Baron W.
key_cases.holding: ICWA's active-efforts and serious-damage requirements in 25 U.S.C. § 1912(d)-(f) do not apply to a proceeding removing a guardian of an Indian child, and the superior court's removal of the grandmother as guardian, based on the child's best interests, was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Is Alaska's controlling authority on the standard for terminating a minor's guardianship, including for an Indian child.
key_cases.quote: We affirm the superior court's removal of the grandmother as guardian.

key_cases.case_name: Taryn M. v. State, Department of Family & Community Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Denial of an ICWA-preferred relative's request for placement was affirmed because OCS proved by clear and convincing evidence that she was an unsuitable caretaker for a medically fragile child, although the superior court erred in assigning any burden to the relative.
key_cases.relevance: Governs whether a preferred relative can be excluded from becoming the child's permanent caregiver.
key_cases.quote: Because OCS demonstrated by clear and convincing evidence that the relative was an unsuitable caretaker, we affirm the superior court.

key_cases.case_name: In re Adoption of Sara J.
key_cases.holding: The prevailing social and cultural standards of the Indian community do not themselves govern the good-cause determination under ICWA § 1915, but remain relevant to the suitability of a preferred placement and may inform a special-needs good-cause finding; the good-cause findings here were affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Applies to permanency placements achieved through adoption or kin caregiving where ICWA preferences are in play.
key_cases.quote: They may also inform, but need not control, any determination of whether a child's special needs or other circumstances constitute good cause to deviate from the preferences.

key_cases.case_name: Jacob v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Grandparents were entitled to a declaratory judgment that OCS violated their statutory rights to notice of and participation in their grandchildren's CINA proceedings, but their remaining claims — including the request for systemic injunctive relief — became moot once they intervened.
key_cases.relevance: Protects relatives pursuing kinship permanency by guaranteeing notice of permanency hearings.
key_cases.quote: We hold that all other issues are moot due to the Jacobs' subsequent intervention in their grandchildren's CINA proceedings.

extended_foster_care_age: To the 21st birthday by court order only: state custody ends at the 19th birthday unless the court grants one-year extensions past 19, which require the person's consent and a best-interests finding, and a person already released from care may ask the court to resume custody before the 21st birthday (Alaska Stat. § 47.10.080(c)(1)(B), § 47.10.080(v), § 47.10.100(a))

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met
